**Q2. Community composition: what structures it more, climate or disturbance?**
Hypothesis: Rainfall and dry-season length set the main floristic turnover (evergreen → deciduous). Disturbance shifts plots toward deciduous, non-endemic species.

## 1. Import data
```{r}
#Creating a fuction to read in data
#The data files are in ASCII text, tab delimited
read_tab <- function(file) {
  read.delim(file.path("Data", file), sep = "\t", header = TRUE,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE,
             na.strings = "NA", strip.white = TRUE)
}
#Using the function to import data
macro      <- read_tab("Macroplot_data_Rev.txt")
micro      <- read_tab("Microplot_data.txt")
sites      <- read_tab("Site_variables.txt")
splist     <- read_tab("Species_list.txt")
```

DCA for gradient length, which justifies RDA vs CCA for P4. NMDS (Bray–Curtis) with envfit/ordisurf (e.g. a rainfall surface).
Cluster analysis (hclust, cutree) on Bray–Curtis or Hellinger distances; compare the clusters with ForestType and use envfit species vectors to see which species characterise them. 
PERMANOVA (adonis2) by disturbance and forest type, with betadisper to check dispersion
